Independent bounded direct additive-decomposition and gap-deletion enumeration through genus 14
correctness.rationale: For fixed m and g≥m+1, F≥g>m; the only possible effective generators are the primitive nonzero Apéry representatives w_i=mx_i+i. They are primitive exactly when no nontrivial Kunz inequality with their residue on the right is an equality: a decomposition of w_i cannot use a positive multiple of m, and reducing each summand to its least representative must leave no added multiples of m. If there are no children, the largest representative w_r=F+m is decomposable. If there are at least two, two distinct representatives in (F,F+m] force a coordinate difference in {−1,0,1}. Each resulting equality is an affine hyperplane whose normal is independent of the all-ones genus equation: in a Kunz equality the result index differs from the two summand indices and has opposite sign, even when the summands have the same index. Two independent equations leave at most O_m(g^(m−3)) integer points by choosing the nonpivot coordinates in [1,g]. A proportional relative box about the balanced slice point gives Ω_m(g^(m−2)) strictly feasible vectors with max x_i<2 min x_i, and all positive compositions give the matching upper bound for N_m. For m≥4 use a proportional box on x₁=x₂ at the indicated positive profile; x_d (d=m−1≥3) has coefficient one in the remaining sum equation, so there is no congruence obstruction. The two tied maxima w₁,w₂ differ by one and are both primitive and effective. For m=3 the explicit even- and odd-genus pairs differ by one and two in Apéry value, also both effective for sufficiently large genus. Hence T_m, and therefore B_m, have the matching lower order for all sufficiently large g. At m=2 the unique semigroup has generators 2,2g+1 and F=2g−1, giving exactly one child when g≥2. A separate bounded tree enumeration, starting at the empty gap set with F=−1 and recursively adding each indecomposable present integer greater than F and ≤F+m+1 (m first positive nongap), gave the genus-14 profiles by degree for m=3: [0,4,1,0], m=4: [5,11,6,1,0], and m=5: [13,15,10,4,1,0]. Those are checks, not evidence for asymptotic extrapolation.
residual_risks: Constants, threshold genera, and probability bounds are for fixed m; the argument does not imply a simultaneous all-multiplicity estimate at fixed genus or a sharp leaf count.

evidence: DiPasquale–Gillespie–Peterson report prior eventually quasipolynomial fixed-m, fixed-g enumeration and asymptotic density one of maximum embedding dimension at fixed m. The cited original Kunz article was inaccessible via the tested route.
The internal-semigroup framework classifies internal versus leaves, not the frequency of every degree, and the indexed fixed-F two-to-one inequality examined applies at m=4.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A lattice-point framework and eventual quasipolynomial form do not alone identify the exceptional set as codimension one, nor prove a nonzero multiple-child term of that order in every large genus. The known maximum-embedding property does not control near-ties at the top of the Apéry set.

evidence: Prior m=3 and m=4 results genuinely give or sharpen those cases. Prior geometry supplies the Kunz parametrization and analytic counting framework. The new proof uses both Kunz-equality and coordinate-near-tie loci, and a positive open part of the two-highest-coordinate tie slice entirely within strict Kunz inequalities.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Counting only Kunz boundary faces misses multiple effective generators at maximum embedding dimension. To deduce the stated sharp error for every fixed m one must also count near-ties and prove a positive-dimensional lower-bound family with integer points for all large genera, which the checked sources do not supply.

evidence: Casas–Madrid–Rosales identify children as removals of a minimal generator greater than F; one-child is an exact effective-generator count, not a minimal-generator count without the cutoff.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Changing from tree degree to number of right generators preserves the claim. Changing to embedding dimension does not: even completely primitive Apéry representatives can give either one or more generators above F.

evidence: At m=4, the two-child profile gives e₂(g)=3g/5+O(1) and e₃(g)=1 for g≥4; a companion fixed-genus record gives L₄(g)=13g/30+O(1), N₄(g)=g²/12+O(g). Thus these records imply T₄(g)=3g/5+O(1) and P₄(μ=1)=1−62/(5g)+O(g⁻²).
The same-day fixed-F record 19b1a83db8fa is a different statistic and quantification. The frozen all-m theorem is itself an indexed hit, not distinct coverage.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The m=4 specialization really is covered with stronger constants; it is not merely a numerical table or a family with a different effective-generator definition. The specialization cannot settle arbitrary fixed m.

originality.rationale: The main contribution is the sharp error order for one child and the matching multiple-child count for every fixed multiplicity, not the total count, maximal embedding dimension, or the small-m cases. Earlier indexed m=4 results are quantitatively stronger in that single multiplicity, and the primary m=3 theorem directly covers the exceptional child cases there. None of the checked statements furnishes the joint all-fixed-m law, including a matching lower bound for every sufficiently large genus.
residual_risks: The original Alhajjar–Russell–Steward full text remains inaccessible via the tested routes. Low multiplicities and total-enumeration ingredients are prior; historical priority for the all-m effective-degree result remains bounded by the inspected sources.

value.rationale: It identifies the typical branching degree in a standard semigroup tree and gives the sharp exceptional probability across all fixed multiplicities, stronger in interpretation than a qualitative leaf/internal comparison. The multiple-child lower bound separates the phenomenon from merely counting degenerate Kunz boundary points and explains why maximal embedding dimension is insufficient.
residual_risks: Does not prove a global internal-versus-leaf conjecture uniform over multiplicity or give leading constants for general m.
